chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Imran al-Hamadhani, who said:

There were five hundred dinars due from me to al-Nahiyah, and I became distressed because of it. Then I said to myself: I have shops which I bought for five hundred and thirty dinars; I have made them for al-Nahiyah for five hundred dinars, though I did not utter this.
So he wrote to Muhammad ibn Ja'far: Take possession of the shops from Muhammad ibn Harun for the five hundred dinars that are owed to us by him.

key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: a designation for the sacred authority to whom the debt was owed
key_terms.الَّتِي لَنَا عَلَيْهِ: which is owed by him to us
key_terms.حَوَانِيتُ: shops or commercial properties owned by the narrator

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam’s knowledge of an unspoken intention regarding a financial debt?
ai.summary: This report narrates that Muhammad ibn Harun inwardly resolved to transfer his shops in settlement of a debt owed to al-Nahiyah. A written instruction then came confirming that very arrangement, indicating knowledge of his unspoken intention and the acceptance of the property against the amount owed.
